description: Create an event-triggered automation workflow from a node/edge graph. Created as a DRAFT — verify it with volanea_test_workflow, then activate explicitly via volanea_update_workflow { status: 'active' }. Idempotent by name. Triggers: "event:<name>" (a product event sent to POST /v1/events or the volanea_track_event tool), "contact.created", "segment:enter:<segmentId>", "segment:exit:<segmentId>".

graph.description:
Automation graph. Exactly one `trigger` node is the entry point; edges connect node ids. Node types and their `config`:
- trigger: entry node, no config.
- send_email: { templateId? } and/or { subject?, body? (HTML), fromEmail?, fromName? } — template fields fill anything omitted.
- delay: { minutes?, hours?, days? } (defaults to 1 minute if all omitted).
- wait_event: { event: "<eventName>", timeoutHours? (default 72) }. The unlabeled outgoing edge fires when the event arrives; an edge labeled "timeout" is taken on timeout.
- condition: { conditions: <same condition tree as segments> }. Outgoing edges must be labeled "yes" and "no".
- update_contact: { set: { <customField>: value, ... }, subscribed? }.
- webhook: { url, payload? } — POSTs workflow/contact context to your URL (5s timeout).
- exit: ends the walk.
`x`/`y` are canvas coordinates for the dashboard editor — space nodes out (e.g. x = index * 260, y = 80).

label.description: Branch label — "yes"/"no" for condition nodes, "timeout" for wait_event.

name.description: Workflow name. Acts as the idempotency key.

reentry.description: Whether a contact can re-enter: never, after finishing a previous walk (default), or always.

name: volanea_create_workflow

code.description: Machine-readable failure code to branch on. Present only when success is false.

note.description: Where to read the full graph back.

status.description: Created as draft — a draft enrols no one until activated.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason. Present only when success is false.

success.description: False when the call failed; read `error` and `code` in that case.
